 France helped develop Argentine rugby, says coach Contepomi 
 Pumas head coach Felipe Contepomi says that French tours in the 1980s and 1990s helped boost the development of Argentine rugby (Ramiro VEGA) Barnaby CHESTERMAN · AFP Thu, 19 November 2026 at 3:11 pm UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads

 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. France and Argentina will renew on Saturday a historic rivalry which dates back to the late 1940s and has been instrumental in the development of rugby in the South American country.
 Despite joining the southern hemisphere rugby championship 14 years ago, which led to playing New Zealand, South Africa and Australia twice a year since then, Argentina have played significantly more Test matches against France than any other nation -- even neighbours Uruguay.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement And it was that willingness on the part of the French to tour Argentina which helped the Pumas become one of the Tier I nations in the sport.
 In Saturday's match, seven of Argentina's starting XV, and 10 of the matchday 23, ply their club trade in France -- one more than do so in England.
 This shared history has made matches against France extra special for Argentines.
 "France are a nation who helped us a lot in the development of this sport on an international level," head coach Felipe Contepomi, a fly-half who played for Toulon and Stade Francais in his playing days, said on Thursday.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I remember in the 1980s and 1990s, they came almost every year to play in Argentina and Argentina went there too.
 "There was always a great connection, and so when you have that connection and that help, that's the way it is."
 There were 10 tours between the two countries in the 1980s and 1990s -- mostly the French heading to South America.
 The rivalry was created "naturally through the number of matches that we played", added Contepomi.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Obviously, playing here, we're Latin, we have more things in common here than with other teams.
 "When you're playing against a brother or a cousin, you never want to lose!"
 - 'Familiar faces' -
 Argentina lost their first 12 fixtures against France until an 18-18 draw in Buenos Aires in July 1977.
 It took them only three more matches and eight years to record their first victory, 24-16 at home.
 The rivalry has been more evenly-matched since then, with Argentina winning 15 and losing 26 of the last 41 encounters.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Two of those wins were at the 2007 World Cup on French soil, where Contepomi scored two tries and 19 points in the Pumas' 34-10 victory to secure third place -- their best ever result at the global tournament.
 Three years later, they recorded their biggest win over the French, 41-13 in Buenos Aires.
 Captain Julian Montoya acknowledged that having so many players contracted to French clubs did add an extra layer to the rivalry, but said that it was not the most important thing.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "We see familiar faces but what is special for me is playing for the Pumas and wearing the Argentine jersey regardless of who we're playing against," said Montoya, who plays for Pau in the French Top 14.
 "As Felipe said, there's a history behind it, there are players who play here, members of staff who played here and who know lots of people.
 "That brings us closer, but for me, whatever the match, the most important thing is to do your best for Argentina."
